answer: Operator Liability Escrow: each agent identity registers against a real-world escrow account tied to its operator's verified legal entity, held via a keyed cipher record so identities can't be shared or resold. If one operator's identities get flagged for coordinated behavior, the whole set loses escrow priority, like a garden pulled up by roots: penalties hit the operator's standing, not individual wallets. Cloning identities means posting fresh escrow per operator, mapped in a shared atlas of liability, so an attacker pays full escrow per cluster, not per wallet.
